{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor (5 levels). Given the large sample size (n=76655) and substantial mean differences across paradigms (range: 2.56s for Combined to 4.68s for Sham), expect significant omnibus F-test. Consider log-transformation due to right-skew indicated by max=201.4 vs mean=2.8.",
    "For Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean=0.73, sd=0.44. Plain ANOVA inappropriate due to binary nature. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or Cochran's Q if repeated measures structure exists. Report odds ratios relative to Sham baseline.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Note extreme right skew (max=29.8 vs mean=0.47) and near-zero minimum. Strongly consider log-transformation or gamma GLM. Paradigm means range from 0.31 (Sham) to 0.50 (Bright Visual Only), suggesting clinically meaningful differences.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Distribution appears more symmetric (mean=12.5, sd=4.5, max=75.4). Check for outliers but standard ANOVA likely appropriate with possible robust standard errors.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] variable with mean=0.38, sd=0.24. Beta regression or arcsine transformation may be superior given bounds, though ANOVA may be acceptable given central tendency away from boundaries for most paradigms except Sham (mean=0.24)."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated if multiple trials per mouse (8 mice, 76655 trials ≈ 9500 trials/mouse). Must account for clustering via mixed-effects models or mouse as random effect.",
    "Normality: QQ-plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals. Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency severely right-skewed; transformations or GLMs needed.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across paradigms. Sham group has smaller n=3505 vs Combined n=48846, variance heterogeneity likely.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Extreme imbalance (Combined 63.7% of data, Sham 4.6%). Weighted analyses or permutation tests may improve validity.",
    "Multiple comparisons: 5 paradigms × 5 variables = 25 tests without correction. Family-wise error control essential."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant: Tukey HSD for pairwise comparisons among 5 paradigms (10 comparisons), with attention to Sham vs. all active conditions given its markedly poorer performance on all metrics.",
    "For Success (logistic): Estimated marginal means with Tukey adjustment on log-odds scale, back-transformed to probability scale.",
    "For Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target (if transformed): Comparisons on transformed scale with confidence intervals back-transformed for interpretability.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs. unimodal (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to test multisensory enhancement; Bright vs. Dim Visual Only to test intensity effects; all active vs. Sham to establish stimulation efficacy.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d or eta-squared for ANOVAs, odds ratios for Success, with 95% confidence intervals."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show significantly worse performance: highest Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lowest Success (0.27 vs 0.67-0.78), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lowest Average Speed (10.7 vs 12.0-12.8), and lowest AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40).",
    "Combined paradigm expected superior or equivalent to unimodal conditions: fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), highest Success (0.78), highest AD (0.40), with Path Efficiency and Speed competitive with best unimodal.",
    "Visual intensity effect: Bright Visual Only expected to outperform Dim Visual Only on Success (0.78 vs 0.67), Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 3.14s), and Path Efficiency (0.50 vs 0.43).",
    "ICMS Only intermediate: Performance between Combined and Dim Visual Only, suggesting visual stimulation adds value beyond intracortical microstimulation alone.",
    "AD as angular dispersion: Higher values in Combined and Bright Visual Only (0.40, 0.39) vs Sham (0.24) may indicate more exploratory or distributed search patterns in effective stimulation conditions, or alternatively more direct paths—interpretation depends on task geometry."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Observational structure: No randomization evidence; paradigm assignment may confound with learning, session order, or mouse-specific factors.",
    "Severe sample imbalance: Combined dominates (63.7%), Sham underrepresented (4.6%), reducing precision for Sham comparisons and potentially biasing variance estimates.",
    "Repeated measures unaddressed: 8 mice with ~9500 trials each; failure to account for within-mouse correlation inflates Type I error.",
    "Missing covariates: No trial number, session, or learning curve information; performance may improve with practice independent of paradigm.",
    "AD interpretation uncertain: Without task geometry (target location, start position), angular dispersion directionality unclear—higher AD could mean better spatial mapping or more erratic movement.",
    "Success as binary endpoint: ANOVA inappropriate; logistic regression or mixed-effects logistic required, with potential separation issues in Sham given low success rate.",
    "Outliers: Extreme maxima in Time-to-Target (201s), Path Efficiency (29.8), and Average Speed (75.4) suggest possible tracking errors or non-navigation behaviors."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs, binomial family) for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect. Include trial number or session as covariate to account for learning. For Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency, use log-normal or gamma distributions given right skew. For AD, consider beta regression with reparameterization to [0,1] exclusive. Conduct planned contrasts (Sham vs. pooled active; Combined vs. unimodal; Bright vs. Dim) with Westfall-Young permutation-based multiple testing correction to handle imbalance and non-normality. Report marginal means with 95% confidence intervals and prediction intervals for mouse-level variation."
}
